subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The choice defines a scheduled-run tool-access boundary and public config/default contract, including how hard denies interact with existing policy layers and current cron jobs that use direct delivery.

options.title: Add cron-specific policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test upgrade behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions too, reducing config surface while coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Avoid a new global cron policy and rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, documentation, and delivery-mode safeguards for scheduled runs.

recommendation.title: Add cron-specific policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, then document and test upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from prior review context plus recent cron runner and scoped tool-policy foundation work.
